name: Zero

hero.title: Stop choosing between a static site and a server app.
hero.lede: Every page in a Zero app picks how it renders: built once, cached and refreshed, rendered per request, or client-only. One line per page. Loaders, server actions, islands and seven deploy targets come in the same box.

why.title: The parts of a web app you would otherwise assemble.

items.title: One line decides each page
items.text: `export const renderMode = 'ssg'` on the landing page, `'isr'` on the blog, `'spa'` on the dashboard. A layout's choice cascades to the pages under it, and the build prints a table of what each route got.

items.title: Cache the page, not the person
items.text: `serverIsland()` leaves a hole in a cached page that is filled per request: a cart badge, a greeting, a live price. The page around it stays on the CDN, and visitors without JavaScript see the fallback.

items.title: Forms that work with JavaScript off
items.text: `<Form>` renders a real `<form method="post">`. With JavaScript, the same action runs over fetch with `pending()` and the optimistic `input()`. A redirect answers 303, so a refresh never resubmits.

items.title: Server code stays on the server
items.text: A `.server.ts` file next to a route is never imported by the client bundle, and the Vite plugin strips each `defineAction` handler, plus the imports only it used, out of the browser build. Pyreon's own CI builds real apps and fails if a server-only marker turns up in their client files.

difference.title: A form with a server action: three files, or one.

before.label: Next.js App Router
before.caption: A server action file, a client component for the pending state and the error, and the page that renders it.

after.label: Zero
after.caption: One route file. The handler never reaches the browser, and the form works before JavaScript loads.

features.title: Included, configured, and out of the bundle when you don't use it.

items.name: File-system routing
items.text: with layouts, URL-invisible `(groups)`, and `_error`, `_loading` and `_404` files per segment

items.name: Typed routes:
items.text: `typedRoutes: true` makes `<Link href="/postz/1">` a compile error

items.name: Server loaders
items.text: in a `.server.ts` file, fetched in one request per navigation

items.name: Server actions
items.text: with a no-JavaScript fallback, pending state, an origin check and a 1 MiB body limit

items.name: ISR with tag invalidation:
items.text: a webhook calls `revalidateTag('posts')` on the ISR handler, and `createFsStore` survives a restart

items.name: Server islands
items.text: for per-request fragments inside cached pages

items.name: Optimised images, self-hosted fonts, favicons and OG images drawn in JSX,
items.text: plus a service worker that precaches exactly what shipped

items.name: Env validation:
items.text: only `ZERO_PUBLIC_*` reaches the client, and a missing declared variable fails the build

items.name: Sessions, CSP nonces, CORS and rate limits,
items.text: through the same request pipeline in dev and production

api.title: Split by where it runs: the main entry is browser-safe.

groups.name: @pyreon/zero/server (its default export is the zero() plugin)

limits.title: `mode: 'auto'` is experimental
limits.text: Zero can infer each page's mode from its exports. Read the mode table the build prints, and declare `renderMode` on any page where the answer matters.

limits.title: Streaming is opt-in
limits.text: Set `ssr: { mode: 'stream' }`. ISR routes always render buffered, because the cache stores whole responses.

limits.title: More than one server needs shared state
limits.text: The default ISR store is in memory and `createFsStore` is for a single box. Behind a load balancer, plug in a shared store (Redis, KV). From the next release, server-island fragments are signed: set the same `PYREON_ISLAND_SECRET` on every instance.

limits.title: Big static builds multiply
limits.text: Dynamic routes times locales adds up. Use `ssg.concurrency`, `ssg.workers` and `onProgress` on large sites.

comingFrom.title: A route module with a loader and an action
comingFrom.note: The shape you know: the file is the route, and the action sits next to the page. Routes come from the folder with no `routes.ts` to keep in sync, `pending()` and `result()` are signals, and one more line (`export const renderMode`) makes any page static, cached or client-only.

comingFrom.title: A cached page that refreshes itself
comingFrom.note: The refresh interval is set once for the app in `zero({ isr })`, not per page. A `loader` also runs in the browser on client-side navigation; put database code in a `.server.ts` file next to the route instead. On-demand refresh goes by tag: the ISR handler's `revalidateTag('posts')` drops every cached page that rendered posts.

recipes.title: One app, four rendering strategies
recipes.text: Set the default once and override by path. A page's own `renderMode` export still wins over the rule, and the build prints the mode each route resolved to.

recipes.title: A personal cart badge on a cached page
recipes.text: The pricing page is cached for everyone. The badge is fetched per visitor from a fragment endpoint that `createServer` mounts for you, and it renders with the request's locals, exactly like a page.

recipes.title: A server action that validates its input
recipes.text: Pass any Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot, ArkType or `@pyreon/validate`) before the handler. Bad input never reaches it: the action answers 422 with messages per field, and the handler receives typed, parsed data.

faq.a: Zero is pre-1.0: breaking changes land in minor versions with a changelog entry, and `pyreon upgrade --write` aligns your `@pyreon/*` versions and runs the codemod for any break that can be migrated mechanically. pyreon.dev itself is built and deployed with it.

faq.q: How is it different from Next.js?
faq.a: One render pipeline for every mode, so the same loader works in SSR, ISR, SSG and SPA, and the mode is a per-page export. There are no server and client component trees to split. Components run once and update through signals, so there is nothing to memoise.

faq.q: Do I have to use Vite?
faq.a: Yes. Zero is a set of Vite plugins: `pyreon()` compiles the JSX and `zero()` adds routing, rendering and the build. `zero dev`, `zero build` and `zero preview` wrap them.

Node, Bun, Deno, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages or any static host. Leave `adapter` unset and the build picks it from the platform's environment. A route can ask for the edge with `export const runtime`, and the build fails if the adapter can't do it.

faq.q: Is it faster than Next.js on a real app?
faq.a: We don't claim that yet. The repo has a suite that builds the same app with Zero, Next.js, React Router, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Nuxt, Astro, TanStack Start and Qwik City (`bun run bench:stacks`), and no result from it is published. The numbers on this page are component-level server rendering and hydration.
